title: Vision and Image Processing
tagline: Images and vision, from pixels and gratings to the models that see.
intro: Interactive notes built for the classroom. Each page starts from intuition, then adds the maths, figures and live demos that run in your browser. New modules are added as the course grows.

modules.title: Light, eyes and cameras: where an image comes from
modules.summary: From light to three numbers per pixel: the plenoptic function and the slices devices record, the eye as a camera with rods, cones and a blind spot, spectra of lights and surfaces, three cones and metamers, photon counting and shot noise, the Bayer filter and demosaicing, and illusions that show the brain infers surfaces rather than reading pixels.
modules.short: The plenoptic function, the eye, spectra, cones and metamers, photon noise and the Bayer filter.
learn: Every imaging device records only a slice of the plenoptic function
The eye and the camera both reduce a spectrum to three numbers, so different spectra can look the same
A sensor counts photons (noise √n) and sees one colour per pixel through the Bayer filter

modules.title: Images as sums of gratings: the 2-D Fourier transform
modules.summary: The 2-D Fourier transform built up from a single 1-D sinusoid: gratings and wave vectors, the frequency plane, slices and the projection-slice idea, rows-then-columns DFTs, the 8 × 8 Fourier basis, rebuilding a photo grating by grating, reading spectra, the wallpaper view and windowing, magnitude versus phase, filtering, and a lab for your own images.
modules.short: Gratings, the frequency plane, magnitude and phase, windowing and filtering, with live demos on real photos.

pages.title: The 2-D Fourier transform, built from the ground up

learn: A 2-D sinusoid has a frequency and a direction: the wave vector
Every image is a weighted sum of gratings; magnitude says how much, phase says where
Reading spectra, windowing the borders, and filtering by drawing on the frequency plane

modules.title: Where the eyes go: gaze, reading and visual attention
modules.summary: How people actually look: a sharp fovea and a blurry surround, reading as a sequence of fixations and saccades, the perceptual span and the moving-window paradigm, Yarbus's task-dependent scanpaths, gaze as visible attention, pop-out versus serial search, and what 'attention' means in neural networks.
modules.short: Fovea and periphery, reading scanpaths, Yarbus's scenes, visual search, and attention in neural networks.

pages.title: Where the eyes go: how people scan text and scenes

learn: Only a ~2° patch is sharp, so the eyes jump 3–4 times a second
Where the eyes land depends on the task, not only on the pixels
Feature pop-out versus serial search, and how human attention relates to attention in neural networks
